claims: "Heavy-duty overlock" (Amazon renewed listing title; a listing word, not a rating)
conflicts: Warranty: blogs and dealers say 25-year limited with free phone support for life. Brother's warranty PDF gives 1 year parts, labor and accessories, 5 years electronics (labor excluded) and 25 years for the chassis casting only, to the original buyer from an authorized seller. Free lifetime phone support is not in the PDF. We use Brother's terms.
Weight: Brother's page says 12.57 lb; a comparison blog says 13.5 lb; an Amazon listing says 16.4 lb, which reads as shipping weight. We use the Brother page.

Thread conversion: Brother's DX spec table lists 2/3/4 thread change as Yes while the DX copy says 3 or 4 threads, and its 1034D page lists the same row as No. The DX table row may be a data error; we do not claim 2-thread stitches.
Dimensions: Amazon lists 13 x 15.25 x 14.5 in, which is package size. Brother's page gives 13.19 x 11.10 x 11.65 in for the machine without labelling the order.

Price: Brother USA lists the 1034DX at $289.99 and the 1034D at $319.99 on 2026-10-01, so the DX costs less there, the reverse of the usual 'DX costs more' claim. Walmart has listed the DX at $235 in the past.
Stitch length: a comparison blog says the DX lacks the 1034D's 1 to 2 mm narrow and 1 mm roll settings; Brother's page does not say. Listed, not resolved.

ownerThemes.theme: Reviewers describe the DX as the same machine as the 1034D with a brighter LED, a deeper trim trap and dials moved to the right side; opinions on whether that is worth the extra cost are split.
Threading order and the lower looper path are the main hurdle for new owners; walkthroughs say route the lower looper thread left and under the foot.

editorial.verdict: The 1034D with an LED light and 0.9 lb less weight, listed by Brother at $30 less; buy it when it is the cheaper of the two.
editorial.whoFor: A first serger buyer who wants the brighter light and the lighter body and finds the DX at or below the 1034D price.
editorial.skipIf: You want 2-thread stitches (Brother's own pages disagree on this), a quiet machine, or the 1034D is cheaper where you shop.
strengths: Same 1,300 spm, differential feed and three snap-on feet as the 1034D, plus an LED work light and 0.9 lb less weight per Brother's pages.

weaknesses: Threading is the most discussed owner topic: some find it very easy, others cannot keep the upper looper thread in place.
Help threads about tension, chaining and timing are common, though most owners who are happy do not post.
Brother publishes no motor power; two commenters say the DX has 75 W against 100 to 110 W for the 1034D, which is unverified.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Brother 1034DX and the 1034D?
faqs.a: Brother lists the DX at $289.99 and the 1034D at $319.99 on 2026-10-01, so the DX costs less there. On Brother's pages the DX adds an LED work light (the 1034D has a bulb) and weighs 12.57 lb against 13.45 lb, but it lists no accessory storage where the 1034D does. Speed (1,300 spm), differential feed and the three snap-on feet match. Commenters say some parts such as the needle plate differ, so check the part number before ordering spares.

faqs.q: Is the Brother 1034DX a good serger, according to owners?
faqs.a: Owner accounts are split. Of 39 reliability statements in our read, 27 are negative and 10 positive, with owners describing a machine that stopped serging or a repair quote not worth paying, and 7 of 15 threading statements are positive against 5 negative. Reddit leans toward people asking for help, so problems are over-represented. Walmart shows 4.5 from 1,914 reviews (seen 2026-10-01), but that listing pools reviews that name the 1034D, so treat it as a soft figure [verify].

faqs.q: How do you thread the Brother 1034DX?
faqs.a: Brother lists lay-in threading with color-coded guides printed on the machine, and one walkthrough says to route the lower looper thread left and under the foot. Owners are split on how it goes: some call it very easy or say it is hard at first and gets easier, while others cannot keep the upper looper thread in place or rethread many times and still get tangles. Use the manual or the instructional CD in the box for the step order, as we do not give a thread path here.

faqs.q: What is the price of the Brother 1034DX?
faqs.a: Brother USA lists the 1034DX at $289.99 (seen 2026-10-01) and the 1034D at $319.99 the same day. That makes the DX the cheaper of the two on Brother's own store, the reverse of the usual claim. Prices drift, so use the price band on this page as the stable guide.

faqs.q: Is the Brother 1034DX a serger, and does it do 2-thread stitches?
faqs.a: It is a 3 or 4 thread overlock serger with 2 needles. Brother's page lists 22 stitches, including 4-thread and 3-thread overlock, ribbon lock and rolled hem, and the list names no coverstitch. We do not claim 2-thread stitches: Brother's DX spec table lists 2/3/4 thread change as Yes, but the DX copy says 3 or 4 threads and its 1034D page lists the same row as No.

faqs.q: What comes in the box with the Brother 1034DX?
faqs.a: Brother lists a standard foot on the machine, a blindstitch foot and a gathering foot, plus 4 mini spools of thread, a soft cover, an instructional CD, a needle set and a trim trap. It uses standard household sewing machine needles. One new owner found no oil in the box and the oiling instruction deep in the manual.

Brother's limited warranty is 1 year for parts, labor and accessories, 5 years for electronic components and circuit boards (labor excluded) and 25 years for the chassis casting only, to the original buyer from an authorized seller. Free lifetime phone support, which some blogs and dealers mention, is not in Brother's warranty PDF.

faqs.q: Is the Brother 1034DX good for beginners?
faqs.a: It is entry-class, with color-coded guides printed on the machine. Threading is still the most discussed owner topic, and owners report help threads about tension and loose, wobbly edges on a new machine. Plan time for the instructional CD and videos before your first project.

faqs.q: Can the Brother 1034DX do a rolled hem?
faqs.a: Yes. Brother lists the rolled hem as built in. Owner reports on it are few in our read: 2 statements, 1 negative and 1 neutral.
